author: zytri
quote: It took me a long time to settle on my final score, mostly because the hype and marketing surrounding GTA VI have been so relentless over the past few years that I honestly felt somewhat embarrassed for not enjoying the ggame as much as I expected. But putting all that aside, I found it surprisingly lifeless. The graphics are undeniably excellent, but if that's the best the game has to offer after 13 years of development and $2 billion, then it's frankly very little. The physics are surprisingly poor, there are several annoying bugs, and the story's ending feels lukewarm and predictable. Ultimately, GTA VI feels like a game that relies far too heavily on its visuals and reputation to justify itself, and I expected considerably more than this.

author: zytri
quote: A disappointing 4/10. I really wanted to love Planet Coaster 2 as I did with the first game, but it feels like a step backwards in almost every aspect that matters. The building and park management controls have become unnecessarily complex and tedious, turning what used to be a creative and enjoyable experience into a frustrating exercise in navigating menus and managing pointless mechanics. Pool management is an absolute mess, and even building a park with attention to detail no longer feels fluid or intuitive. Instead of encouraging creativity, the game constantly gets in the way of it. What makes things worse is that I honestly don't see a meaningful leap forward in graphics, assets, or overall gameplay to justify these changes. At times, it genuinely feels more like a DLC that somehow makes the previous game worse rather than a proper sequel. Planet Coaster was about creativity and the joy of building your dream amusement park, but this sequel manages to make even that feel like a chore. A huge missed opportunity.

author: zytri
quote: An absolute fun game and one of the biggest surprises I've had in gaming. Dave the Diver is one of those rare games that manages to be incredibly creative, ridiculously fun, and surprisingly addictive all at once. The combination of underwater exploration, fishing, restaurant management, and an ever-growing collection of unexpected activities works brilliantly. There is always something new happening, another mechanic to discover, another character to meet, or another ridiculous situation to get involved in. The amount of content is honestly impressive, and the game keeps introducing new ideas without losing its charm. I especially love the humor, the pixel art, the soundtrack, and how much personality every character has. What starts as a relatively simple diving and sushi restaurant game gradually turns into an incredibly rich adventure full of surprises. It's also one of those games where you constantly tell yourself you'll play for just another 15 minutes and suddenly realize hours have passed. A genuinely brilliant piece of game design that deserves far more recognition. Pure gaming joy.

author: zytri
quote: A fantastic and one of the most refreshing Pokémon experiences in years. Pokopia is such a clever and charming combination of Pokémon, Animal Crossing, and Minecraft, but what really surprised me is how naturally all these elements come together to create something that feels genuinely unique. There is something incredibly satisfying about rebuilding the world, creating habitats, discovering new Pokémon, and gradually turning an abandoned place into a thriving community. The Pokémon themselves are the absolute highlight, each bringing their own personality, abilities, and little interactions that make the world feel alive. I also love how the game rewards curiosity and creativity without constantly pressuring you to progress. There is always something new to discover or another little project that makes you say, "Just five more minutes." My only minor criticism is that some progression mechanics can feel a little repetitive, and the inventory management could be better. Still, this is an incredibly well-crafted, relaxing, and surprisingly engaging adventure. A wonderful new direction for the Pokémon franchise.

author: zytri
quote: A perfect game and, without a doubt, the most immersive game I've ever played. I still remember being absolutely blown away by the sheer scale of the world when I first realized just how much of ancient Greece and its islands Ubisoft had recreated... I was thinking "How this could even be possible?!". The level of detail, geographical accuracy, architecture, landscapes, and atmosphere is simply breathtaking. It genuinely feels like travelling through ancient Greece rather than just playing a video game. I could spend hours sailing between islands, exploring cities, climbing mountains, and discovering hidden places without ever getting bored. The world feels incredibly alive, and the attention to detail makes the experience truly unforgettable. The DLCs are equally impressive, beautifully crafted, and just as ambitious as the main game, adding even more depth to an already extraordinary adventure. For me, Assassin's Creed Odyssey represents the absolute peak of Ubisoft's artistic direction and execution. I honestly don't think they have ever managed to recreate such a convincing, beautiful, and immersive historical world again.

author: zytri
quote: I can absolutely understand why Elden Ring is considered one of the greatest games of its generation, but personally, it never fully clicked with me. The world feels strangely empty and overwhelmingly grey at times, the animations lack polish, and the gameplay feels somewhat outdated, especially when it comes to combat and character movement. I genuinely appreciate the artistic vision and the excellence of its art direction, but I find the actual execution less impressive. Many environments feel like they rely too heavily on reused assets, which takes away from the sense of discovery after a while. That said, the writing and lore are genuinely outstanding, with an incredibly intriguing universe and a level of narrative depth that rewards curiosity and interpretation. I recognize the greatness of the game and what FromSoftware achieved, but I simply didn't enjoy the experience as much as I expected.

author: zytri
quote: Another absolute masterpiece and a well-deserved 10/10. Tears of the Kingdom takes everything that made Breath of the Wild so special and somehow manages to make it even better. The world is incredibly rich, exploration is endlessly rewarding, and the freedom to experiment with the building mechanics opens up possibilities that still feel almost limitless. But what truly makes this game stand out for me is its story. I honestly think it has the best narrative in the entire Zelda franchise so far. It's beautifully told, genuinely emotional, and gives every protagonist a much deeper sense of purpose and importance. By the end, you truly understand the sacrifices, motivations, and individual roles of each character, making the whole journey feel incredibly meaningful. Some moments genuinely hit hard and stay with you long after the credits roll. An extraordinary achievement that proves Nintendo still knows how to deliver something truly special!
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom

author: zytri
quote: A perfect 10/10 and one of the most magical gaming experiences I've ever had. Breath of the Wild completely redefined what an open world can be. The sense of freedom, exploration, discovery, and adventure is something truly special. Every mountain makes you curious about what's waiting on the other side, every hidden location feels like a personal discovery, and the world constantly rewards your curiosity without holding your hand. The atmosphere, music, art direction, and environmental storytelling come together beautifully to create a world that feels alive and unforgettable. What I love most is how naturally the game encourages you to experiment, explore, and create your own adventures. It doesn't just give you a huge map to explore, it makes you genuinely want to get lost in it. Even years later, few games have managed to capture that same feeling of wonder. An absolute masterpiece that deserves every bit of its legendary status!
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild

author: zytri
quote: An absolute masterpiece and a new standard of excellence for the entire gaming industry. With over 1,000 hours played, I can honestly say that Baldur's Gate 3 still manages to surprise me. Every new playthrough feels like stepping into a different world, and I still keep discovering places, interactions, dialogue options, and details that I had never encountered before. The level of freedom, depth, reactivity, and attention to detail is simply incredible. The choices genuinely matter, and the sheer number of possibilities makes every playthrough feel unique. It's the kind of game that reminds you what video games can achieve when creativity and ambition come together. My only minor criticism is the lack of voice acting in other languages, which would make the experience even more accessible and immersive. Other than that, it's an extraordinary achievement!

author: zytri
quote: A truly outstanding game and easily one of the best RPGs I've played in recent years. Clair Obscur has an incredible world, a fascinating story, unforgettable characters, and some of the most intriguing lore I've ever experienced in a game. The art direction, soundtrack, combat system, and overall atmosphere are simply fantastic. I was completely drawn into its universe, constantly wanting to discover more about its mysteries and the world behind them. My only real criticism is that a few storylines and lore elements are left somewhat unresolved, especially considering how rich and fascinating the narrative is. I would have loved a little more closure and a few extra answers. Still, that's a relatively small flaw in an otherwise exceptional experience!

author: zytri
quote: A masterpiece. I honestly got emotional playing this game. They really understood what made the original so special, keeping everything that deserved to be preserved while improving other aspects in ways that make the experience even better. It feels familiar in all the right ways, but also fresh, beautiful, and deeply moving. You can tell this was made with genuine respect and love for the original. And the Portuguese voice acting is another absolute highlight, adding even more personality and emotion to an already unforgettable experience. They truly got it right. What a beautiful game!
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time
